question.question: Does the actual PrepareReply transport preserve the acceptor value-ballot context used to select prior state during recovery?
question.importance: Losing prior-value context can affect which command and attributes recovery carries into subsequent formation; cluster-level safety consequence remains unestablished.
contexts: Fixed-membership EPaxos, live process, nonzero prior value ballots
event_paths: handlePrepare -> replyPrepare -> SendMsg -> Marshal -> New/Unmarshal -> prepareReplyChan -> handlePrepareReply

supporting_behavior_ids.B-formation: PreAccept or Accept produces the local vbal and value reported by handlePrepare.
supporting_behavior_ids.B-config: Participant IDs and N determine concrete ballot values.

counterevidence: Ballot itself is transmitted and replies must match lastTriedBallot.
VBallot zero is preserved for zero-valued inputs; not every message is affected.
Local recovery self reply relabels vbal and may independently dominate selection.
unknowns: Whether this representation defect changes a decision in a legal full recovery history remains independent; the observed NOOP restart is confounded by self-reply relabeling.
question.trigger_rationale: Exploration 18fb7d1363fa40c1aa157f28b2038356 executed actual proposal, PreAccept, recovery request and Prepare producer. It observed stored vbal 1 and decoded VBallot 0 for the same acceptor/instance. A fixed field-preservation check can resolve this local responsibility without attributing the separately confounded NOOP restart to the codec.

obligation.description: For a PrepareReply emitted by handlePrepare and successfully decoded through the implementation transport without corruption, the decoded VBallot must equal the stored value ballot reported by the producer for the same acceptor and instance.

scope.description: Value-ballot preservation across the PrepareReply transport, for producer-established live instance state in fixed-membership volatile EPaxos.
assumptions: Non-Byzantine producer and uncorrupted complete message bytes.
Producer is handlePrepare after an actual PreAccept-established state; observation is of the same reply and instance.
excluded: No assertion that the prior preaccepted command must be selected or committed.
No cluster agreement violation, client completion failure, automatic recovery trigger or crash-restart guarantee.
No attribution of recovery self-reply relabeling to serialization.

grounding.derivation: This is a composed interface responsibility grounded in the implementation, not an external protocol assertion: handlePrepare explicitly puts inst.vbal in PrepareReply.VBallot while keeping joined inst.bal separately; handlePrepareReply requires the latter for attempt qualification and compares the former to select prior command/attributes/status. Transport must deliver the reported value context unchanged for that consumer meaning. Neither the same-ballot guard nor the independent local self-reply behavior defines a conversion of remote VBallot to zero. New/Unmarshal on the actual network path provides no reconstruction. The requirement is message fidelity, not eventual selection of every reported value.
grounding.applicability: Applies to a successful codec round trip of the actual handlePrepare response under complete byte delivery. Fixed check uses a real producer prefix; sockets, asynchronous scheduling and scanner trigger are outside this local responsibility.
alternatives: A zero-valued input will agree with a zero-initialized decoded field; this does not establish preservation of nonzero values.
Self-reply relabeling can independently affect recovery selection, so consumer NOOP output is not this obligation oracle.

B-wire.rationale: Replace the unresolved producer/preservation premise with the composed interface relationship: handlePrepare reports stored vbal, whereas fresh decode does not restore it. Retain the independent decision-history question.
B-wire.preserves: Principal Fact identity and meaning remain producer-reported context; Candidate still asks transport preservation. No prior obligation or observation scope is changed.

rationale: Ground a narrow transport obligation following producer-backed exploration; do not promote exploration to property Evidence or infer consensus violation.

feedback.answered: Under the controlled three-node prefix, owner 1 produced a PUT PreAccept, acceptor 2 established PREACCEPTED_EQ at vbal 1, and recovery 0 produced Prepare ballot 3. The acceptor retained vbal 1 and reported one command, ballot 3/status 2; decoding the actual reply yielded VBallot 0 while those other observed fields matched. The consumer subsequently restarted a NOOP at ballot 3. The latter is not a codec-only causal result: startRecoveryForInstance separately stamped its empty self reply with value ballot 3. No command had been decided in this prefix.
remaining: Execute a separately fixed field-preservation check and review correspondence.
Decision-level consequences and natural trigger reachability remain outside the codec obligation; self-reply relabeling is an independent sourced question.
feedback.rationale: Actual execution excludes the explanation that nonzero remote value ballots cannot be produced on the inspected path. It does not establish a lost decision or retroactively create Evidence.
